setting: A short lecture in a biology class about how migratory birds find their way across long distances.
narrator_intro: Listen to part of a talk in a biology class.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Every year, millions of birds travel between breeding grounds and wintering sites.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Some species fly thousands of kilometers, often at night and over open water.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: How do they navigate? Researchers think birds use several cues at once.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: The position of the sun and stars can serve as a compass for daytime and nighttime flights.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Many birds also sense Earth’s magnetic field, which gives them a sense of direction even when skies are cloudy.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Landmarks matter too: coastlines, mountain ranges, and rivers help experienced birds stay on route.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Young birds sometimes learn routes by following their parents on the first journey.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Climate change and city lights can disrupt these systems, causing birds to arrive late or become disoriented.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: So migration is not one trick—it is a toolkit of celestial, magnetic, and landscape cues.

talk.speaker: speaker1
talk.text: Next week we’ll look at tracking studies that map exact migration highways.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: How migratory birds navigate over long distances
options.B: How to build birdhouses for city parks
options.C: Why birds never leave their nests

questions.explanation: The professor explains multiple navigation cues birds use during migration.

questions.narrator_text: According to the professor, what can serve as a compass for daytime and nighttime flights?

options.C: The position of the sun and stars
options.D: The sound of ocean waves alone

questions.explanation: She says sun and stars can serve as a compass day and night.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—not mentioned as the compass.

questions.narrator_text: What does she say many birds can sense?
questions.explanation: Many birds sense Earth’s magnetic field for direction when skies are cloudy.

questions.narrator_text: What does the professor imply about bird navigation?

options.A: Birds rely on only one cue for every trip
options.B: Young birds never learn from parents
options.C: City lights improve navigation for all species
options.D: Migration uses a combination of celestial, magnetic, and landscape cues
